Doug Jones

Democratic candidate for Governor, Alabama · Open seat

Attorney; former U.S. senator and former U.S. attorney

Doug Jones is a former U.S. senator from Alabama and a former U.S. attorney. He launched his campaign for governor in Birmingham and is the Democratic nominee for the November 3, 2026 general election, running against Republican nominee Tommy Tuberville. The seat is open because Republican Gov. Kay Ivey is term-limited.

Where Jones stands

Data centers / AI
Proposes a one-year moratorium on new hyperscale data center construction while the state sets rules on power, water, noise and tax incentives. Says companies should pay their own costs and communities should have the final say.
Affordability / taxes
Supports temporarily suspending Alabama's gas tax and eliminating the state's 2% grocery tax. Says housing and costs must be addressed over the long term.
Health care / Medicaid
Supports expanding Medicaid in Alabama. Argues the state has missed out on health care funding and that expansion could help struggling rural hospitals.
Crime / public safety
Opposes deploying the National Guard to Birmingham, Montgomery and Mobile, saying the Guard is not trained for law enforcement. Proposes cooperation among local, state and federal law enforcement, plus more training and resources.
Education / school choice
Proposes phasing out the parts of the CHOOSE Act that pay for private school expenses with public money, while keeping assistance for homeschooling families. Says public education should get the investment.
Lottery / gambling
Supports letting Alabama voters decide on a state lottery. Would also support a broader gambling bill but says he would push for a lottery even if a larger package fails.
Prisons
Calls for an independent review of the Department of Corrections and says he would consider pausing another planned mega prison. Supports parole and reentry changes and settling lawsuits over prison conditions.
IVF / reproductive health
Proposes constitutional protections for IVF and contraception.
Elections / government reform
Supports ending straight-ticket voting and pushing for early voting in Alabama.
